scope: Manual review of all eleven remaining p2483 interfaces, with source-preserving edge-copy and latent-mixture conventions.

rows.query: Search correlated Erdos-Renyi, permutation mixture and Bernoulli graphs; inspect binomialRandom, uniform finite law, bind and Bernoulli parameter orientation.
rows.result: The marginal graph law and uniform permutation mixture have components; the correlated aligned-edge pair law must be supplied.
rows.gap: The correlated graph model still needs a feasible bivariate Bernoulli edge law and its conditional product mixed over the hidden uniform permutation.

comparisons.D1: Given pi, sample iid aligned pairs (A_ij,B_pi(i)pi(j)) for i<j with marginal q and covariance rho q(1-q), then average over a single uniform pi. Marginal binomialRandom alone does not generate the pair correlation. Feasible rho lies in [-min(q/(1-q),(1-q)/q),1]; negative rho is allowed, and rho squared above a threshold does not waive feasibility. Preserve loop-free symmetry and conditional, not unconditional, independence of aligned pairs.

rows.query: Inspect binomial random graph, product measures and latent mixing for the null/alternative graph-pair experiment.
rows.result: The null is the product of two binomial graph laws; the alternative requires the correlated construction while retaining the same marginal laws.
rows.gap: The testing experiment still needs the correlated alternative joint law and proofs of its two Erdős–Rényi marginals.

comparisons.D2: Q denotes the independent null law and P the permutation-mixture alternative, with the same n and q and the same single-graph marginals. A difference in marginal density is not the test signal. Ordinary product represents Q only; conditional pair independence under pi must not be mistaken for independence of the observed graphs under P.

rows.query: Inspect adjacency matrix and expectation semantics under binomial graph marginals; compare centered edge weights with centered subgraph counts.
rows.result: The zero-one adjacency matrix and finite expectation give the centered matrix entrywise.
rows.gap: The centered matrices still need their model expectation, subtracting q only off the diagonal.

comparisons.D4: For simple graphs E A_ij=E B_ij=q when i differs from j and zero on the diagonal, so centered diagonal remains zero. Center the individual edge entries before multiplying in W_H; this is not raw subgraph count minus its expectation. Equal marginal graph laws make the centering the same under P and Q; q is supplied, not estimated by an unmentioned plug-in procedure.

rows.query: Inspect graph isomorphism abbreviation, subgraph-copy cardinality and unlabeled-copy semantics in Maps/Copy.
rows.result: Graph isomorphism matches the adjacency-preserving bijection, and copyCount counts actual isomorphic subgraphs rather than labelled injections.
rows.gap: The combined notation still needs explicit isomorphism classes and automorphism cardinalities with the paper's no-isolated-vertex subgraph convention.

comparisons.D3: Iso G H is a vertex bijection preserving adjacency both ways; aut(H) is the finite cardinality of Iso H H. copyCount G H has host first and pattern second, unlike sub(H,G). The library's subgraphs permit chosen vertex subsets and non-induced edge subsets; enforce the paper's edge-induced/no-isolated-vertex convention in use. Isomorphism classes forget labels and roots; neither graph embedding into a host (induced) nor number of injections is the copy count.

rows.query: Search unlabelled tree families and inspect connected-acyclic tree predicate and graph isomorphisms.
rows.result: Tree structure and isomorphism are available; a fixed-size quotient family still needs construction and finite enumeration.
rows.gap: The tree family still needs one representative per unrooted isomorphism class with exactly K edges.

comparisons.D5: Use connected acyclic graphs with K edges, hence K+1 vertices, and quotient labels by graph isomorphism. Do not use rooted trees, spanning trees of a fixed host or all labelled graphs, which have different counts. The asymptotic regime has K tending to infinity and nontrivial trees, so the no-isolated-vertex convention applies; no executable free-tree generator follows from IsTree.

rows.query: Search Otter constant and unlabelled tree enumeration in graph/probability sources; inspect available tree and isomorphism definitions.
rows.result: Tree and isomorphism infrastructure can specify the counted objects, but no Otter growth theorem was located in the searched revision.
rows.gap: The unrooted tree enumeration limit and its identification with the reciprocal Otter constant still need proof.

comparisons.D9: The limit is |T_K|^(1/K) as the number K of edges grows, for unrooted unlabeled trees. The approximate decimal 0.33833 is not the exact constant or a certified interval, and Cayley labelled-tree enumeration does not supply this limit. Formalizing the family cardinality, existence of the limit and its positive reciprocal is additional to the tree predicate.

rows.query: Inspect factorial permutation count and source tree-copy normalization; compare beta's factorial ratio and signed correlation power.
rows.result: Permutation cardinalities supply factorial counting infrastructure, but the exact statistic normalization remains a source-specific scalar expression.
rows.gap: The scaling factor still needs its exact factorial ratio with valid tree size and signed correlation power.

comparisons.D7: Retain (rho/(q(1-q)))^K times (n-K-1)!/n!, requiring integer K with K+1<=n for the intended factorial counting. Natural truncated subtraction must not manufacture a value for oversized K. q is strictly between zero and one; beta can be negative for negative rho and odd K, unlike the alternative mean involving rho^(2K). No automorphism factor is already absorbed into beta.

rows.query: Search weighted subgraph counts and inspect copyCount's subgraph-cardinality body and graph isomorphism.
rows.result: Unweighted copies are directly counted; replacing each copy's unit contribution with its edge-weight product requires a weighted sum.
rows.gap: The weighted count still needs one product per edge-set copy with a proof of its unweighted specialization.

comparisons.D6: Enumerate subgraphs S of complete K_n isomorphic to H and multiply one M_ij for each undirected edge, then sum once per copy. Do not sum labelled injections (which multiply by aut(H)), require vertex-induced copies, square edges through both orientations, or subtract an expected raw count. For no-isolated-vertex patterns, binary host adjacency yields copyCount G H; arbitrary real/centered weights can yield signed terms and need not define a probability graph.

rows.query: Search signed tree correlation statistic and compare copy multiplicities using inspected unlabelled subgraph counts and isomorphisms.
rows.result: Graph classes and unweighted counts support part of the construction, without a matching weighted cross-graph test statistic.
rows.gap: The statistic still needs centered weighted counts and one automorphism-weighted term per unrooted tree class with the exact beta scaling.

comparisons.D8: For each class [H] use beta aut(H) W_H(Abar) W_H(Bbar), then sum over the K-edge tree family. Keep the separate automorphism multiplier because each W_H counts edge-set copies once. The class term must be representative-independent. Negative rho affects beta's sign; replacing counts by raw unsigned or standardized counts, or enumerating all labels, changes the statistic and its normalization.

rows.query: Inspect little-o at infinity and logarithm domain; compare exact sparse/dense graph regime and maximum denominator.
rows.result: Asymptotic predicates can express the sequence constraints, but no graph-detection theorem establishes this parameter regime.
rows.gap: The regime still needs its integer diverging tree-size sequence, exact logarithmic maximum bound and a precise subpolynomial sparsity formulation.

comparisons.D10: n min(q,1-q)>=n^(-o(1)) is symmetric in sparse/dense complements and allows q varying with n. K tends to infinity and is at most log n divided by max{16 log log n,2 log(1/[n min(q,1-q)])}; preserve max rather than min or sum and handle only the valid large-n logarithm domain. rho^2>alpha is strict and subject to feasible Bernoulli correlation; no uniform theorem for a gap approaching zero or equality at the Otter threshold is supplied.

rows.query: Search alternative mean and tree-test threshold; inspect expectation and counted tree/isomorphism objects against the source scaling.
rows.result: The threshold is an expressible scalar once the alternative-mean identity and tree family are established, but that mean formula was not found in the library.
rows.gap: The threshold still needs the correlated-model expectation identity yielding rho to the power 2K times the number of tree classes.

comparisons.D11: C is fixed with 0<C<1 and tau=C E_P f_T=C rho^(2K)|T|, nonnegative even when rho is negative. It uses the exact statistic's alternative expectation, not the null mean, approximate statistic's empirical mean or bootstrap calibration. Theorems use non-strict errors on both sides at the threshold while the preceding detection definition uses a strict alternative event; preserve the original directions.
